java.finding: Java accepts one anchored braced USymbol command with package, rectangle, hexagon, node, artifact, folder, file, frame, cloud, action, process, database, storage, component, card, queue, and stack, then passes the exact symbol to USymbols.fromString before gotoGroup.
USymbols.fromString maps action, hexagon, and process to distinct USymbolAction, USymbolHexagon, and USymbolProcess identities.

rust.finding: Rust records the complete command-symbol inventory in DeploymentContainerSymbol, but DeploymentContainerSymbol::renderer_kind projects Hexagon, Action, and Process to DeploymentNodeKind::Node.
The parser now recognizes braced command keywords and fails closed when a braced line does not match the anchored grammar, but it stores the renderer kind projection on each node.

The deployment renderer was searched for container_symbol, DeploymentContainerSymbol, Action, Process, and Hexagon consumption. No renderer path consumes container_symbol, so no-oracle output cannot preserve the Java USymbol painting for action/process/hexagon containers.

findings.finding: Every fresh valid Java-success heldout has diff_one --no-oracle exit 1. Rule 10 says any such nonzero diff rejects the parity change with no out-of-scope exemption.

The implementation preserves action/process/hexagon command identity only as parser metadata, while the product renderer still paints them through DeploymentNodeKind::Node. This does not match Java's USymbolAction, USymbolProcess, or USymbolHexagon rendering path.
The b83502c7 inline-empty-leaf behavior is not supported by the Java oracle for the fresh controls: Java exits 200 while the frozen Rust binary exits 0 on all four controls.
